task_signatures.pattern: Drug-disease contraindication identified from patient history
task_signatures.correct_strategy: Identify the clinical condition from patient symptoms first, then check each drug for contraindication in that condition; prioritize over drug-drug interactions
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: Jumping to drug-drug interactions without first diagnosing the condition implied by the patient's history

task_signatures.correct_strategy: Evaluate OTC drugs mentioned in the patient narrative against the full prescription list for clinically significant interactions
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: Only evaluating prescription-to-prescription interactions and ignoring OTC drugs

task_signatures.correct_strategy: Treat specific symptom triggers (sensory, positional, temporal) as diagnostic signals that point to a condition; use that condition to drive contraindication checking
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: Treating patient story details as irrelevant background and proceeding directly to the drug list

failure_modes: missing_clinical_diagnosis: reading prescription list without first interpreting patient symptoms as a diagnosis
flavor_text_dismissal: treating symptom triggers and context clues as irrelevant story details
wrong_priority: reporting a minor drug interaction when a more serious contraindication exists
incomplete_history_read: not reading the full patient narrative before evaluating medications
key_principles: Always diagnose the clinical condition from the history before evaluating the drug list
Drug-disease contraindications take priority over drug-drug interactions
Symptom triggers and context clues are diagnostic signals, not flavor text
Give one recommendation only: the most clinically significant finding
